description:
## Symptom

`fixtures2/00430_opaque_value_accessor.fz` fails on both `fz2 run` and `fz2 interp` with `function_clause`. Reduction: `@type t :: opaque any`; `def get(h :: t), do: :ok`; `main` calls `A.get(1)` — same failure. Without `opaque`, or without the annotation, it runs.

## Mechanism

- `resolve.rs:150-160` publishes an opaque type as `opaque_of(tag)`, a pure nominal tag; the inner type is dropped.
- `dispatch_reachability.rs:136-184` intersects the argument type with that tag, gets empty, and `executable_facts.rs:487-501` materializes zero clauses.
- Nothing in the language produces a value of type `t`, so a parameter annotated with an opaque type can never match.

## How Elixir does it (`../elixir` 759443e72)

`@opaque` is a typespec only (`lib/elixir/pages/references/typespecs.md:241`, `kernel/typespec.ex`): "the internal structure of the type will not be visible, but the type is still public." There is no runtime tag. The value is its underlying structure; opacity is a contract enforced outside the defining module, and inside it the structure is visible.

## Direction

An opaque type is its inner type with the structure hidden outside the declaring module, not a tag disjoint from every value. `Types::mint_owned_resource_aliases` (`types/mod.rs:1418-1429`) has no callers and is an earlier attempt at this; it goes or becomes the mechanism.

## Done when

00430 runs on run/interp/build without a deferral, and the reduction above runs.
title: An opaque-typed parameter admits no value, so its clause is unreachable
